![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14238679/assets/d0f6f5ed91981e15d2fb80e2630cec6d20f566feb627899f529e07bab12b73fb.png)

Consider the vector field $F=⟨{z}^{2},\,2y,\,{x}^{2}+y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by the bounding region of a right circular cylinder of height $2$ whose base is a circle of radius $1$ centered at the origin, as shown above. Given that $S$ is positively (outward) oriented, use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ through $S.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+y) \\  & =0+2+0 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid cylinder enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2\,\text{d}V \\  & =2{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =2\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =2\cdot \pi \cdot {1}^{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =4\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
